A.	Facility Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies

Dutch Tech, Inc. (Dutch Tech) is a foam insulation manufacturing facility located in Lobelville, Tennessee. The facility began operation in December 2023. Dutch Tech is strongly committed to protecting facility personnel, the public, and the environment from workplace and accidental release hazards. This commitment is demonstrated by our comprehensive accidental release prevention program that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training. It is our policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances. Unforeseeably, if such a release does occur, our emergency response policy requires immediate notification of the proper authorities and evacuation of the affected area. Safety, environmental protection and risk management programs are fully implemented and coordinated with the Perry County Emergency Management Agency, LEPC, and other community emergency responders for emergency planning and response efforts.

B.	Description of Stationary Source and Regulated Substances Handled

The Dutch Tech facility manufactures foam insulation with a reflective backing for use in building construction. The plant operations include a polyolefin foam production line, which employs isobutane as a manufacturing aid. Polyolefin foam insulation is a plastic product made of polyolefin resin that can be produced in various widths and rolled to different lengths. This process involves mixing resin with talc, and other additives; extrusion of the mixed resin through a highly specialized plastic extruder; adding a blowing agent (isobutane); then cooling the material and forcing it through a die. The storage quantity of isobutane at the Lobelville facility exceeds the RMP threshold of 10,000 pounds. Isobutane is a flammable gas that is stored in a 12,000-gallon pressurized tank at approximately 40 psi. The isobutane storage a

nd piping system also includes a low-pressure pump station, unloading station, high-pressure pump system, and gas detection devices.

C.	General Accidental Release Prevention Program and Specific Prevention Steps

Isobutane is a regulated substance under both the EPA RMP and OSHA process safety management (PSM) rules. Therefore, Dutch Tech has developed a comprehensive program to meet the requirements under the RMP and PSM standards. Key components of the accident prevention and safety program include: Safety information; Hazards review; Operating procedures; Training; Equipment maintenance program; Management of change; RMP compliance audits; Accident/incident investigation; Routine physical safety audits.

The facility is designed in accordance with NFPA-30 (Standard for Storage and Handling of Flammable and Combustible Liquids). Per the RMP Program Level 3 requirements a Process Hazard Analysis program has been developed. This analysis is performed to identify, evaluate, and control the hazards involved in the process. 

For safely managing the plant production activities, Dutch Tech maintains written operating procedures. These procedures address all modes of operation including initial startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, emergency operations, normal shutdown, and startup after a turnaround. The information is regularly reviewed and is readily accessible to operators involved in the processes. 

The employee training covers the following aspects of health and safety program: safety philosophy, general safety rules, reporting of safety hazards, emergency procedures, and hazards communications. In addition to the training received upon employment, further training is given if an employee is exposed to a previously unrecognized hazard, or if an employee is reassigned to a job that involves exposure to new hazards. 

The safety manual contains documentation of safe work practices, health and safety hazards, descriptions of the use a

nd care of personal protective equipment, and emergency procedures in case of spills or releases. The safety manual also covers the emergency and first-aid procedures. Records for all employees are maintained documenting that each employee has received and understood the required training. 

Dutch Tech carries out and documents maintenance checks on process equipment to ensure proper operations. Process equipment examined include, among others, isobutane storage vessel, piping systems, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, and controls and pumps. The equipment maintenance activities are carried out by qualified personnel. These personnel are offered specialized training, as needed. Any equipment deficiencies identified by the maintenance checks are corrected in a safe and timely manner. 

Written procedures have been developed at Dutch Tech to manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment, and procedures. Process operators, maintenance personnel, or any other employees affected by the modification in process conditions are promptly made aware of changes and provided the necessary training. 

RMP compliance at the facility will be monitored through an RMP audit performed at least once every three years in accordance with 40 CFR 68.79. A report of the findings will be generated following the audit, and any deficiencies and/or recommendations are promptly addressed and documented. 

Procedures on incident investigation, reporting, and documentation have been developed in accordance with 40 CFR 68.81. Investigation details of any incidences will be documented using RMP requirements. 

Dutch Tech believes that process safety management and accident prevention is a team effort. Company employees are strongly encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements. In addition, employees have access to all information created as part of the facility's implementation of the RMP program, including info

rmation resulting from process hazard analyses.

D.	Five-year accident history

There have been no accidents at the Dutch Tech facility.

E.	Emergency Response Program

Dutch Tech has developed an integrated emergency response program that complies with the RMP and PSM requirements. The emergency response plan includes: 
* Procedures for informing the Perry County LEPC and the community about any accidental releases;
* Documentation of first-aid and emergency medical treatment necessary to treat accidental exposure; and
* Procedures for emergency response after an accidental release of isobutane and isopentane.

The emergency management plan is reviewed annually to reflect changes at the facility and to ensure that employees are informed of the changes. Employees are trained periodically on emergency response procedures.

F.	Planned Changes to Improve Safety

No changes to the safety procedures or methods are required at this time. Any procedural changes will be implemented in the future based on the audit findings or revaluation of process hazards.
